candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: PublicationIssue
candidates.embedding_doc_text: PublicationIssue (Thing > CreativeWork): A PublicationIssue is a CreativeWork representing a part of a successively published periodical or publication volume, often numbered and containing a grouping of works. Also called journal issue, magazine issue, periodical issue.
candidates.comment: A PublicationIssue is a CreativeWork representing a part of a successively published periodical or publication volume, often numbered and containing a grouping of works. Also called journal issue, magazine issue, periodical issue. Examples: "Nature" Vol. 500, Issue 1; "The New Yorker" October 26, 2023 issue; a specific issue of a scientific journal. Distinct from PublicationVolume, which is a larger grouping of issues.

candidates.label: PublicationVolume
candidates.embedding_doc_text: PublicationVolume (Thing > CreativeWork): A PublicationVolume is a CreativeWork representing a part of a successively published periodical or multi-volume work, often numbered and potentially spanning a time period. Also called journal volume, book volume, periodical volume.
candidates.comment: A PublicationVolume is a CreativeWork representing a part of a successively published periodical or multi-volume work, often numbered and potentially spanning a time period. Also called journal volume, book volume, periodical volume. Examples: "Nature" Volume 500; "Encyclopedia Britannica" Volume 1; a year's collection of a magazine. Distinct from PublicationIssue, which is a smaller, more granular part of a volume.

candidates.label: Season
candidates.embedding_doc_text: Season (Thing > CreativeWork): A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season.
candidates.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

types.oie_definition: A classification or grouping of websites based on their content or purpose.
types.embedding_query_text: Website Category: A classification or grouping of websites based on their content or purpose. Also called site type, web classification, online category.

final_chosen_type.label: WebsiteCategory
final_chosen_type.definition: A classification or grouping of websites based on their content or purpose.
final_chosen_type.justification: No Schema.org candidate represents a category of websites; existing candidates are for websites themselves or classification codes, not descriptive categories.

candidates.label: WebSite
candidates.embedding_doc_text: WebSite (Thing > CreativeWork): A collection of related web pages and other items, typically served from a single domain. Also called website, internet site, web presence.
candidates.comment: A collection of related web pages and other items, typically served from a single domain. Also called website, internet site, web presence. Examples: schema.org, Wikipedia, The New York Times website.

candidates.label: CategoryCode
candidates.embedding_doc_text: CategoryCode (Thing > Intangible > DefinedTerm): A defined term representing a specific code within a classification system. Also called classification code, item code, type code.
candidates.comment: A defined term representing a specific code within a classification system. Also called classification code, item code, type code. Examples: UNSPSC code for office supplies, NAICS code for manufacturing, a product category ID.

candidates.label: WebPage
candidates.embedding_doc_text: WebPage (Thing > CreativeWork): A single document or resource accessible via a web browser, typically part of a larger website. Also called web document, HTML page, internet page.
candidates.comment: A single document or resource accessible via a web browser, typically part of a larger website. Also called web document, HTML page, internet page. Examples: a product page on an e-commerce site, a news article page, a contact us page.

candidates.label: CategoryCodeSet
candidates.embedding_doc_text: CategoryCodeSet (Thing > CreativeWork > DefinedTermSet): A creative work that defines a collection of related category codes. Also called classification system, code list, taxonomy.
candidates.comment: A creative work that defines a collection of related category codes. Also called classification system, code list, taxonomy. Examples: The UNSPSC classification, a company's internal product category list, a set of industry codes.

candidates.label: PhysicalActivityCategory
candidates.embedding_doc_text: PhysicalActivityCategory (Thing > Intangible > Enumeration): PhysicalActivityCategory is an enumeration for categories of physical activity, organized by physiologic classification. Also called exercise type, activity classification.
candidates.comment: PhysicalActivityCategory is an enumeration for categories of physical activity, organized by physiologic classification. Also called exercise type, activity classification. Examples: AerobicActivity, StrengthTraining, Flexibility. Distinct from PhysicalActivity, which is an instance of an activity.
